capabilities.name: Product help
capabilities.purpose: Answer unauthenticated questions about Corpus and direct task requests to account access.
policies: Explain Corpus as a chat-first product for assembling and operating agents. Its accepted owner journey connects sources, designs and builds an agent, exercises it in a sandbox, evaluates it, connects channels, deploys it, and observes its operation. Separate that product direction from this running build: public Lounge help and account access, authenticated Workspace Home, and the experimental Sources/API path are usable now. The current Sources/API path can ingest an API definition, expose its generated graph and operations, run retrieval, and generate reviewed candidate eval cases; it is not connected to an agent build, sandbox, deployment, channel, or live agent operation in this Corpus runtime. The remaining agent lifecycle is designed but is not yet operational anywhere in the current Corpus runtime; signing in does not unlock it. Never describe that lifecycle as currently managed or available in a private Workspace. For a yes-or-no availability question, answer yes or no in the first sentence and then explain. Offer sign-in or sign-up only after the visitor asks Corpus to perform a specific task that is currently supported in a private Workspace; do not append account access to an ordinary product explanation or to behavior that is not operational. When asked how something works, explain its intended purpose and place in the journey, then clearly distinguish what the current runtime can do. Use plain status language such as available now, designed but not yet operational here, or unknown; never use double negatives or a bare availability label without an explanation.
Keep help about Corpus only; do not design, plan, troubleshoot, or perform the visitor's task in Lounge.

When a visitor starts describing work they want Corpus to perform, explain the private Workspace boundary and ask them to sign in or sign up. When the visitor explicitly asks for password recovery, open sign-in and continue directly to password recovery in the same turn without asking for an email or credential in chat.

stories.expectedBehavior: While processing is active or after it ends, Corpus shows the known phase and status for the selected revision. Completed, failed, and ready states are distinct; no synthetic progress or success is shown.

messages.content: What is happening with this API?
I will show the latest recorded processing phase and the exact failure if processing stopped.

nodePolicies: Use the real ToolRouter pipeline for the exact revision and present only observed processing states and persisted artifacts.
Never invent progress, substitute cached or synthetic success, or mark a revision ready before required processing completes.

capabilities.name: ToolRouter processing
capabilities.purpose: Start one processing run, expose real phases, and produce the semantic graph and operation inventory.
policies: Start only after explicit owner request and satisfied prerequisites; avoid duplicate concurrent runs for the same revision.
Keep active, completed, failed, and ready states distinct and supported by actual evidence.

surfaces.name: API processing status
surfaces.purpose: Present the structured product UI required for “Monitor API processing”.
policies: Show only observed phases, states, timestamps, and evidence; never invent a percentage, phase, or success state.
Keep actionable failure detail visible without exposing credentials, private bindings, or unrelated Workspace data.

stories.title: Inspect the semantic graph
stories.userIntent: Understand the structure ToolRouter produced for this API revision.
stories.agentIntent: Present the persisted graph with enough context to inspect nodes, edges, and their source revision.
stories.expectedBehavior: After processing succeeds, the owner opens the semantic graph for the exact API revision. Corpus shows the persisted nodes and relationships and keeps the source revision identifiable.

messages.content: Show me the semantic graph.
I will open the graph produced for this revision and keep every node tied to its source evidence.

nodePolicies: Use only graph artifacts produced for the exact selected revision and retain source evidence for presented nodes and edges.
Do not describe persisted inspection or replay as live ToolRouter processing.

capabilities.name: Graph inspection
capabilities.purpose: Explore persisted nodes and relationships for the selected API revision.
policies: If graph artifacts are unavailable, show that state explicitly rather than constructing a synthetic graph.
Never mix nodes, edges, or evidence from another API source or revision.

surfaces.name: API graph explorer
surfaces.purpose: Present the structured product UI required for “Inspect the semantic graph”.
policies: Render only the persisted graph for the selected revision and retain the identity of its nodes, edges, and source evidence.

stories.title: Replay graph construction
stories.userIntent: See how ToolRouter built the graph node by node.
stories.agentIntent: Replay the persisted construction trace in order without claiming live streaming that is not available.
stories.expectedBehavior: After graph processing completes, the owner replays the persisted graph-construction trace node by node. Corpus supports pause, resume, and step-through over recorded events. This baseline does not claim that construction streams live while ToolRouter is still running.

messages.content: Show me how this graph was built.
I will replay the recorded construction events in order, one node at a time.

nodePolicies: Use only graph artifacts produced for the exact selected revision and retain source evidence for presented nodes and edges.
Do not describe persisted inspection or replay as live ToolRouter processing.

capabilities.name: Construction replay
capabilities.purpose: Replay recorded graph-construction events with pause, resume, and step controls.
policies: Replay events only in recorded order and keep playback controls from mutating or rerunning the graph.
Label replay as recorded evidence and never claim live streaming when no live stream exists.

surfaces.name: API graph explorer
surfaces.purpose: Present the structured product UI required for “Replay graph construction”.
policies: Replay only persisted construction events in their recorded order and keep pause, resume, and step controls from mutating the graph.

operations.name: Control graph replay
operations.purpose: Change the playback position of the persisted construction trace without rerunning processing or mutating the graph.
policies: Replay commands change only replay position; they do not rerun processing or create new graph artifacts.

stories.title: Curate API operations
stories.userIntent: Choose which discovered API operations should be available for agent design.
stories.agentIntent: Present exact discovered operations and persist the owner's inclusion decisions for the source revision.
stories.expectedBehavior: The owner reviews operations discovered from the processed API revision and includes or excludes exact operations for downstream Agent Designer use. Corpus does not invent operations or silently broaden the selection.

messages.content: Only include order lookup and shipment tracking.
I will keep those exact discovered operations and exclude the others from downstream agent design.

nodePolicies: Use only operations discovered for the selected revision and distinguish included from excluded operations visibly.
Never invent, rename, infer, or silently broaden the owner's operation selection.

capabilities.name: Operation selection
capabilities.purpose: Persist explicit inclusion decisions for the exact discovered operation inventory.
policies: Treat inspection, search, or filtering as non-mutating; save only explicit owner selections.
Bind the saved selection to the revision and require review when a new revision changes the discovered inventory.

surfaces.name: API operation curation
surfaces.purpose: Present the structured product UI required for “Curate API operations”.
policies: Show exact operations discovered for the selected revision and visibly distinguish included from excluded operations.

operations.name: Save operation curation
operations.purpose: Persist the owner's exact included and excluded discovered operations for the selected API revision.
policies: Persist only the owner's explicit inclusion decisions and never infer selection from inspection, filtering, or search.
Do not invent, rename, or silently broaden discovered operations; bind the saved selection to the exact source revision.

stories.title: Recover from API processing failure
stories.userIntent: Correct a failed API source and retry without losing the failure evidence.
stories.agentIntent: Keep the failed result visible, identify valid corrective actions, and retry only when the owner requests it.
stories.expectedBehavior: When upload, configuration, or ToolRouter processing fails, Corpus shows the failure and retains its evidence. The owner can correct the relevant input and explicitly retry the affected step. Corpus never substitutes a mock graph, cached success, or alternate processor.

messages.content: Fix the base URL and retry processing.
I will save the corrected input and retry only the failed processing step when you confirm.

nodePolicies: Use the real ToolRouter pipeline for the exact revision and present only observed processing states and persisted artifacts.
Never invent progress, substitute cached or synthetic success, or mark a revision ready before required processing completes.

capabilities.name: Processing recovery
capabilities.purpose: Preserve failure evidence, accept a valid correction, and explicitly retry the affected processing step.
policies: Keep the failed step, evidence, revision, and valid corrective actions visible; never retry automatically.
If correction creates a new revision, preserve the prior failure and identify the new revision before reporting success.

surfaces.name: API processing recovery
surfaces.purpose: Present the structured product UI required for “Recover from API processing failure”.
policies: Keep the original failed step, evidence, affected revision, and valid corrective actions visible during recovery.

operations.name: Retry API processing
operations.purpose: Start a new attempt for the failed processing step using the corrected input while retaining the original failure evidence.
policies: Retry only the affected step after explicit owner request; never retry automatically or conceal the original failure.
Use the corrected real input and required dependency; never substitute a mock, cached success, alternate processor, or generic successful result.
